My soaring spirits freeze solid in an instant.

Gooseflesh races over my body, and my throat forgets how to breathe.

Goosebumps form all over my body, and my throat won’t move as if it’s forgotten how to breathe.

重ねた指が強く握られる。
俺が逃れようのない死を感じているように。
セイバーもまた、覆しようのない絶望を、その身に感じ取っていた。

“…………Shi… rou…”

Saber, behind me, must feel it too.

Her fingers tighten around mine.

—Just as I sense a death from which there can be no escape,

Saber feels a despair that nothing can overturn.

“…Shi… rou.”
It must be the same for Saber behind me.
Her hand holds me tightly.
Just as I feel an unavoidable death.
Saber too feels an inconcealable desperation.

“I have kept you waiting, Saber.

“As promised, I have come to claim you.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I have kept you waiting, Saber.
I have come for you as promised.”

…His voice sounds like it’s sneering.
Haughty and merciless.
I can feel no human emotion in his arrogance, nothing that has ever considered the opinions of others.

Imperious. Merciless.

In that arrogance, as though he has never once considered what anyone else might want, there is no trace of human feeling.

This close.

At a distance where battle could begin at any moment, a presence more steeped in death than Berserker stands waiting.

“Whoever you may be, you could never have assembled the Noble Phantasms that stand as the symbols of other heroes. No such Heroic Spirit exists in this world.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Are you insulting me, Archer? That is even more impossible.
No matter who you are, it would be impossible for you to collect all the Noble Phantasms, the symbols of other heroic spirits. No such heroic spirit exists.”

Saber is right.

Every Noble Phantasm he possesses is genuine.

There is a demonic sword from the legends of northern Europe, and another from somewhere in South America.

No hero ever ranged across so much of the world. And more fundamentally—Gae Bolg belongs to Lancer alone.

All the Noble Phantasms he has are real.
There are demonic swords from Northern Europe, and demonic swords from South America.
No hero made his name in so many different places. And first of all, only Lancer has Gae Bolg.

By that rule, anyone who possesses Gae Bolg must be the spear's owner—Cú Chulainn.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Heroic spirits’ Noble Phantasms are the weapons they had when they were alive.
By that rule, as soon as he has Gae Bolg, he has to be Cu Chulainn.

There would at least be an explanation if all his Noble Phantasms were imitations. But if they are originals, this contradiction……………………………………………………………

No. Wait.

Originals—the weapons that came *before*…?

pages.en:
“—It can't be. But…”

No. It is possible.

Legends and myths did not spring from nothing.

Every mythology shares certain elements because somewhere, there was an original from which they descended.

A legend becomes complete as a faith only after taking root in its own land. Perhaps demonic and holy swords gain their powers in the same way.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“It can’t be. But, wait…”
It is possible.
Myths and legends do not start from nothing.
All myths have common points because a single foundation became their model.
Because legends that become objects of faith are only those that originate in that land. I think demonic swords and holy swords start having special abilities around that time.

What if every object called a Noble Phantasm in later myth once existed in an earlier form, before it acquired that name—?

My limbs—my entire body—have recovered only enough for my fingers to twitch when I clench my teeth.

“Genuine. Is that what you mean?

“Yes, Saber. The tale is simple.

“Let us speak of the most ancient age, when the world was still one.

“There was a prosperous nation whose king gathered every treasure beneath the heavens.

“Nothing lay beyond his reach. Nothing was absent from his wealth.

“The king possessed a perfect treasury. The countless weapons within it went unused and entered their long sleep beside him.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Real, right?
Yes, it is really simple, Saber.
Let me tell you about the most ancient time, when the world was still one.
That kingdom flourished, and the king collected every treasure in the world.
There was nothing he could not collect, and he lacked nothing.
The king had a perfect treasury, and the masses of weapons in there were never used, but instead went to sleep with the king.”

“After the king's death, the contents of his treasury scattered across the world. Being peerless weapons, they were prized and put to heroic use, until in time they came to be revered as Noble Phantasms.

“…Do you understand now, King of Knights?

“The Noble Phantasms you wield were nothing more than that king's property to begin with.”

After the king’s death, the contents of the treasury room spread all over the world. They were valued because they were splendid swords, and they eventually became Noble Phantasms.
…Do you understand, king of knights?
The Noble Phantasms you use are just the king’s possessions.”

pages.en:
…They are an inheritance.

Trace any lineage or history far enough into the past, and there must be a prototype.

It follows that the myths, legends, and Noble Phantasms of every land must have some primal form at their source.

And if, in that distant past, someone had been able to gather those prototypes—then that person would have owned every Noble Phantasm.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…It’s like inheritance.
If you go back far enough, a “model” must exist.
So it is only natural for every legend, myth, folklore, and Noble Phantasm to have an original model.
Andin the distant past, if it was possible to collect all of their models, then one could possess all of the Noble Phantasms.
